economy.summary: Voted for House Bill 1500 of 2023, which would raise Pennsylvania's minimum wage in stages to $15 per hour; the bill passed the House 103-100 in June 2023.
economy.short: Voted to raise state minimum wage to $15 per hour.

taxes.summary: Voted in June 2026 to end Pennsylvania's sales and use tax exemption for computer data center equipment, a measure that passed the House 197-5; she said the incentive is no longer needed given the growth of data centers and that the revenue can support education, property tax relief, and infrastructure.
taxes.short: Voted to end data center equipment sales tax exemption.

abortion.summary: Voted against Senate Bill 106 of 2022, a proposed package of constitutional amendments that included language stating the Pennsylvania Constitution does not grant any right to abortion or to taxpayer funding of abortion; the measure passed the House 107-92.
abortion.short: Voted against no-constitutional-right-to-abortion amendment package in 2022.

education.summary: Supported the 2026 state budget, citing a $670 million statewide increase for public schools that includes $565 million in adequacy funding and $121 million for school safety and mental health grants; she said she was proud to support a budget that prioritizes students.
education.short: Supported 2026 budget increasing public school and adequacy funding.

healthcare.summary: Reintroduced House Bill 534 of 2023, which would cap patients' out-of-pocket insulin costs at $35 for each 30-day supply; she said the bill would reduce the financial burden on people who rely on insulin.
healthcare.short: Sponsored bill capping out-of-pocket insulin costs at $35 monthly.

energy.summary: Voted for House Bill 2224 of 2026, which passed the House 202-0 and would limit investor-owned utilities' returns on equity and eliminate the 6% gross receipts tax on electricity sales, with utilities required to pass the savings to customers; this addresses electricity rates rather than a broader energy or environmental platform.
energy.short: Voted to limit utility profits and cut electricity tax.

guns.summary: Voted for House Bill 714 of 2023, which would require background checks for private sales and transfers of long guns; the bill passed the House 109-92 in May 2023.
guns.short: Voted for expanded background checks on long gun sales.
